description: Institutions frequently did not believe children's disclosures, particularly where the accused denied them; some chose to preserve the alleged perpetrator's reputation and their own above protecting children; concerns were not escalated and information not shared, recorded or acted on.
energy_note: They were told. They decided the other way.

aspect: EXAMPLE - policies existed and were not followed
description: Despite significant safeguarding policies being in place, these were not upheld, and inaction or institutional complacency allowed perpetrators to continue undetected. Review recommendations often went unimplemented.
energy_note: The policy was fine. Nobody applied it.

aspect: EXAMPLE - moved on rather than reported
description: Institutions reacted to disclosures by moving perpetrators on without investigating or reporting - which transferred the risk to a different set of children and removed the record.

aspect: EXAMPLE - disputing that safeguarding applied to them
description: Some individuals disputed that they held 'positions of trust' and therefore claimed safeguarding policies did not apply to them - an argument about scope, advanced in place of an answer.
energy_note: Arguing about whether the rules covered him.

aspect: The structural risk factors are known
description: Quality of staff relationships, staffing ratios, establishment size, physical environment, training and openness to external input all affect risk - meaning the conditions are modifiable and were not modified.
energy_note: Known, listed, and not acted on.
